name: Beef Steak Ramen with Soft-Boiled Egg
description: Seared rump steak, wheat noodles, pak choi and spring onions in a beef, soy, garlic and ginger broth, topped with a soft-boiled egg.
instructions: Bring a small saucepan of water to the boil. Carefully lower in the egg and cook for 6½ minutes. Transfer it immediately to cold water, then peel and halve it.

Pat the steak dry and season it with salt and black pepper. Heat 1 tsp neutral oil in a frying pan over high heat and sear the steak for approximately 2–3 minutes per side, depending on its thickness and your preferred doneness.
Transfer the steak to a board and rest it for at least 5 minutes. For medium-rare steak, aim for approximately 52–54°C after resting.
Add 500 ml water and the beef stock cube to the saucepan. Add the crushed garlic, grated ginger, 1 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp dark soy sauce and 1 tsp honey. Simmer gently for 8–10 minutes.
Add the noodles and cook according to their packet instructions. Halve the pak choi lengthways and add it for the final 2 minutes.
Remove the broth from the heat and stir in 1 tsp rice vinegar and 1 tsp sesame oil. Taste before adding any extra salt.

Slice the rested steak thinly against the grain. Divide the noodles, pak choi and broth into a deep bowl, then arrange the steak and soft-boiled egg on top. Finish with finely sliced spring onions, black pepper and the steak's resting juices.

substitutions.label: Use ribeye steak
substitutions.note: Cook the ribeye exactly as described for the rump steak, adjusting the frying time for its thickness.
